text: Under a coordinate change xⁱ → x̃ʲ(x), how do the components of a covector (one-form) α = α_i dxⁱ transform in this book?
choices: α̃_j = (∂x̃ʲ/∂xⁱ) α_i, the same rule as a contravariant vector.
α̃_j = (∂xⁱ/∂x̃ʲ) α_i, with the inverse (transpose) Jacobian of the vector rule.
α̃_j = α_j; covector components are coordinate-invariant.
α̃_j = (∂x̃ʲ/∂xⁱ)(∂x̃ᵏ/∂xˡ) α_i, with two Jacobian factors.
explanation: Covectors (lower, covariant indices) transform with the inverse Jacobian ∂xⁱ/∂x̃ʲ, while vectors (upper, contravariant indices) use ∂x̃ʲ/∂xⁱ; because the two matrices are inverses, the pairing α_i vⁱ is an invariant scalar. Choice 0 is the vector (contravariant) rule, choice 2 wrongly asserts invariance of the components, and choice 3 carries the index structure of a (0,2) tensor rather than a single covector.
